narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

Much clearer than yesterday; temperatures and winds little changed. Dry until evening showers, with thunder possible from midday, peaking this evening. 30°C (87°F) high, 19°C (67°F) low. Sky clear early as reported, mostly clear at midday and mostly clear in the evening. Wind NNE early, WSW at midday and SW in the evening; gusts to 36 km/h (20 kt). UV index 8.9 (very high). Air quality 90 (moderate) at Ochieng' Avenue, Kisumu Central, the highest of 3 stations. As of 06:01, reports through 05:00: no rain; no thunder; high so far 22°C (72°F); low so far 19°C (66°F); peak sustained 7 km/h (4 kt); sky clear.

## Extended Outlook

Temperatures and winds much the same through Thursday, with showers and thunderstorms likely each day. Skies partly cloudy Tuesday and Wednesday, then mostly cloudy Thursday. Thursday's call: rain, 54%, with two of four models wet; highs around 30°C (86°F). Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) calls it wet. At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 90% of the time over 96 checks.

Further out, temperatures and winds much the same through Monday, with showers and thunderstorms likely Friday, dry Saturday with thunderstorms likely, and dry Sunday and Monday with thunderstorms possible. Friday: three of four models wet, highs 29 to 32°C (85 to 89°F). Saturday: two of four models wet, highs around 31°C (88°F). Sunday: two of three models wet, highs 30 to 32°C (85 to 90°F), thunder possible rather than likely.

Only GFS, ECMWF and ICON reach past Saturday. Monday's call: dry, 0%, with no model wet; highs around 31°C (88°F). At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 93% of the time over 94 checks.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

Convective instability in the hours ahead: UKMO 2500 J/kg, ECMWF 1660 J/kg, ICON 1420 J/kg and GFS 1250 J/kg. Thunder likely; any thunderstorm brings sudden gusts well above the 36 km/h (20 kt) forecast.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

Peak gust 30 km/h (16 kt). Any thunderstorm brings sudden gusts well above this figure; the water is unsafe while one is nearby.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the north (1009 hPa) and highest toward the northeast (1016 hPa) — a 7 hPa spread, a moderate large-scale gradient. Pressure is also falling toward the south — a large-scale feature building in that direction, though this sampling cannot say how fast or whether it will reach here. Pressure overhead is near-steady. Sampling is a nine-point ring at 12-degree spacing, so this locates a direction, not a centre or a front. Across the basin's 5 points, pressure today sits between 1012.8 and 1015.2 hPa, near-steady over three days (-0.2 hPa). Pressure here over the last 24 hours: +0.2 hPa.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

On rain the record ranks ECMWF first at Day+3, right 90% of the last 30 checks and ECMWF first at Day+7, right 93% of the last 30 checks. On today's high UKMO is the warmest model at 30.4°C (86.7°F) and GFS the coolest at 29.6°C (85.3°F); the call's 30.5°C (86.9°F) sits at the warm end. Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) calls a high of 30.0°C (86.0°F) and rain, agreeing with the call on rain. At Day+0, no model is meaningfully better than the others here yet. At Day+3, ECMWF is the strongest rain caller here and kenya_met the weakest. At Day+7, ECMWF is the strongest rain caller here and GFS the weakest.

Figures issued 06:01. Written by code; a discussion follows when a model answers.
